entries.title: A01 (Weakening / Positive Implicative Axiom; K-Axiom; Russian: Утверждение следствия)
entries.notes: Positive implicative weakening axiom (K-combinator type). sections.title: Predicate logic
sections.description: First-order predicate calculus with typed domain, Bernays rules, substitution, and eigenvariable conditions.

entries.title: Discourse domain is non-empty
entries.notes: Layered axiomatization: Section 2 axiomatizes pure First-Order Predicate Logic over sort Class prior to Section 3 (Class Comprehension). In multi-sorted / inclusive predicate logic (where some sorts like Nonstored / Void are uninhabited), 2.01 explicitly postulates that the sort Class is inhabited so (∀(K : Class) φ) → (∃(K : Class) φ) holds in pure predicate logic; once Section 3's Class Comprehension Axiom (3.01) is added, 2.01 becomes derivable (witnessed by ∅).

entries.title: Exists Abstraction (EA / Bernays)

entries.title: Generalisation (Gen)

sections.title: Set/class-theoretic foundations of mathematics
sections.description: Morse–Kelley (MK) axiomatic class theory with Dunaev tagged ordered pairs, class comprehension, class conditional if-then-else, simple_if, if_dep, and Ordinal Induction.

entries.title: Class Comprehension Axiom
entries.notes: In Variant 1 (1st-Order NBG/MK), Class Comprehension is formalized at the metalevel as an axiom schema (class_comprehension_rul / class_comprehension_meta_axm_fm in foundations.ML, entry 4.06) parameterized by an arbitrary formula expression φ : Fm with side condition NFV(v_C, φ). In full Morse–Kelley (MK), φ may contain bound class variables (impredicative comprehension); in pure NBG, φ is predicative (quantifies only over sets) and is finitely axiomatizable via Bernays–Gödel class-existence axioms B1–B7. Lowercase x, y are used by naming convention because elements of classes must be sets (isSet(x)).

entries.title: Subset-Sethood / Heredity Axiom (Subclasses of Sets are Sets)
entries.notes: Subset-Sethood (subclasses_of_sets_are_sets_entry, SML ID 3.12 in foundations.ML): any subclass A of a set b is itself a set (equivalent to the Separation Axiom). Note: this is distinct from Element-Sethood (x ∈ A → isSet(x)), which follows directly from the definition of sethood isSet(x) ⟷ ∃(Y : Class) (x ∈ Y) (SML ID 3.02, set_def_entry) and which Variant 2's Formulas-as-Types surface language exposes as the built-in primitive heredity(x, A) : x ∈ A → Set(x).

entries.title: Regularity (Foundation / Cumulative 𝒫-Induction) Axiom
entries.notes: Axiom of Foundation / Regularity (foundation_entry, SML ID 3.14 in foundations.ML, matching Foundations 060_axioms.tex Definition [foundation]): formalized in the SML kernel in the cumulative 𝒫-induction form ∀(X : Class) ((𝒫(X) ⊆ X) → (V ⊆ X)) (if a class X contains every set whose elements all lie in X, then X contains all sets V), which is classically equivalent (by taking X = V \ A) to the standard ∈-minimal-element formulation ∀(A : Class) (A ≠ ∅ → ∃(x : Class) (x ∈ A ∧ x ∩ A = ∅)).

entries.title: Class Cardinality (|K|)
entries.notes: Initial-ordinal class cardinality (card_def_entry, 3.41 in foundations.ML): for a set K, |K| is the least ordinal a ∈ On into which K injects (K ⪯ a); for a proper class K (where { a ∈ On | K ⪯ a } = ∅ so ⋂∅ = V), |K| = On ∩ V = On.

entries.title: Semi-Singleton Subset Relation (s sss A)
entries.semantic: ∀(s : Class) ∀(A : Class) ((s sss A) ⟷ ((s ⊆ A) ∧ ∀(x : Class) ∀(y : Class) (((x ∈ s) ∧ (y ∈ s)) → (x = y))))
entries.notes: Foundations ch. 110 (Semi-Singleton Subset, sss_def_entry, 3.36 in foundations.ML): binary infix relation (s sss A) asserting that s is a subclass of A with at most one element: (s ⊆ A) ∧ semi_singleton(s). For any class A (whether a set or a proper class), the sets s satisfying (s sss A) are ∅ and {a} for each element a ∈ A; hence their unary union reconstructs A itself: ⋃{ s | s sss A } = A (Theorem 110.1 in 110_family_evaluation.tex). By contrast, extracting the unique element a from a singleton class X = {a} uses unary intersection: Value(X) = ⋂{ y ∈ X | semi_singleton(X) } (Foundations 040_old_variant_of_iota_defs.tex §614 & 190_union_intersection.tex §65), so Value({a}) = ⋂{a} = a whereas Value(∅) = Value({a, b}) = ⋂∅ = V (proper class / nonset).
